title: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister, vows to work with 'humility and honesty'
content:
• Pralhad Joshi has taken charge as the Union Education Minister, replacing Dharmendra Pradhan whose resignation was accepted by President Droupadi Murmu.
• Pralhad Joshi also holds the portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy, in addition to the Education Ministry.
• The change in the education ministry followed a 37-day agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar concerning alleged NEET-UG examination irregularities, which concluded after government assurances.

title: From Smriti Irani to Pralhad Joshi: 12 years, 5 Education Ministers under NDA—a look at their tenures as Pradhan resigns
content:
• Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned due to the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy, and Pralhad Joshi was subsequently given additional charge of the Ministry of Education.
• The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 was approved in July 2020 during Ramesh Pokhriyal's tenure, replacing the 34-year-old National Policy on Education from 1986.
• The Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD) was renamed to the Ministry of Education in July 2020, restoring its pre-1985 name.

title: Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of Education Ministry after Dharmendra Pradhan resigns- Who is he?
content:
• Pralhad Joshi has been assigned the additional charge of the Union Education Ministry.
• Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the Union Council of Ministers, with President Droupadi Murmu accepting his resignation, following protests over the NEET paper leak.
• Union Minister Pralhad Joshi currently also serves as the Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).

title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, FIRs withdrawn, compensation promised: CJP ends protest
content:
• The government committed to providing ₹1 crore as compensation to the families of NEET victims, a primary demand met by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP).
• Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday (25 July) after a 36-day agitation by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak.
• The government agreed to withdraw all FIRs filed against protesters and scheduled further talks with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) within a month (approximately four weeks) regarding broader educational and exam reforms.

title: Time has come to remove this govt: Rahul Gandhi harks 'don't be afraid!' as Dharmendra Pradhan resigns
content:
• Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Education Minister on Saturday, July 25, submitting his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi amidst nationwide student protests.
• The resignation followed weeks of nationwide student protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, with students demanding greater transparency and accountability.
• Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, acknowledged the resignation but continued to demand the Prime Minister's apology and action against police responsible for violence against students during protests, referencing the Jantar Mantar incident on July 20.

title: RBI, govt measures could turn India's balance of payments surplus, ease pressure on rupee: HDFC
content:
• The RBI decided to bear the full hedging cost for fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) deposits until September 30, 2026, with potential inflows of USD 40-60 billion, of which USD 17 billion was already mobilised by July 17, 2026.
• A concessional foreign exchange swap facility for external commercial borrowings (ECBs) by public sector undertakings (PSUs) could attract an additional USD 15-25 billion in inflows.
• The government's decision to withdraw capital gains and withholding tax on returns from investments in government securities could attract USD 10-20 billion over the next 12-18 months, by increasing the likelihood of Indian bonds being included in the Bloomberg bond index.

title: Forex reserves up by $1 billion to $676 billion
content:
• India's forex reserves increased by $1 billion to $676 billion.
• The rupee weakened last week, moving from 95.62 to 96.28.
• Gold reserves decreased by $3.5 billion to $101.7 billion.

title: Isuzu signs five-year pact with Kamarajar Port for vehicle exports
content:
• Isuzu Motors India Pvt. Ltd. has signed a five-year agreement with Kamarajar Port Ltd (KPL) for the export of commercial vehicles.
• Under the new five-year agreement, Isuzu Motors India will receive concessional wharfage rates linked to export volumes from Kamarajar Port.
• Isuzu Motors India has been exporting its D-Max and S-Cab models through Kamarajar Port from its Sri City, Andhra Pradesh facility, to West Asia markets since 2019.

title: India's exports to UK may reach $115 billion by 2030 due to trade pact: Assocham
content:
• India's exports to the UK are projected to reach $115 billion by 2030 due to a free trade agreement, as stated by industry body Assocham.
• The UK free trade agreement came into force on July 15 this year.
• The total trade trajectory between India and the UK is expected to expand from $58 billion in 2025-26 to $115 billion by 2030, along with the possible creation of 7-10 lakh new employment opportunities.

title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns amid massive student protests, Centre moves to clear Jantar Mantar
content:
• The Union Cabinet approved a draft Bill against exam paper leaks, stipulating a jail term up to 10 years, a penalty up to Rs 10 crore, and a five-month timeline for investigation and trial.
• Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, sending his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, amid massive student protests over exam paper leaks.
• Irregularities in the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, 2026, led to its cancellation, an investigation by the CBI, and a re-examination for over 20 lakh students, which was completed on June 21, 2026.
